canonical_spec.title: Mergers, acquisitions and control
canonical_spec.outcome: Evaluate acquisition economics and distinguish synergy from wealth transfers.

assignments.scope: Mergers, acquisitions and control: separate target standalone operating/equity values, improved control value and buyer-specific net synergies; quantify timed operating benefits less integration, taxes, incremental investment and deal costs without counting them twice. Derive buyer NPV, target gain, total surplus and maximum acceptable price with full debt/cash/other-claim boundary. Supply an original cash-deal and fixed-exchange-ratio stock-deal comparison; endogenously reconcile post-deal shares, prices and wealth rather than treating a quoted stock consideration as a fixed cash price. Analyze financing sources/uses, fees, EPS accretion versus shareholder value, purchase accounting versus economic value, execution and conditional closing risk. Treat control premiums as evidence needing an economic decomposition; no universal synergy/premium or current regulatory/legal claims. Include original dataset, exact standard-library lab and eight full solutions.

canonical_spec.title: Private equity, venture capital and entrepreneurship
canonical_spec.outcome: Analyze illiquid ownership structures and financing incentives.

assignments.scope: Private equity, venture capital and entrepreneurship: original dated LBO sources/uses, operating cash available for scheduled debt reduction, refinancing/exit assumptions, equity proceeds and IRR/MOIC with no double-counting principal repayment or treating leverage as free value. Explain entry price, operating growth, multiple change and debt paydown with an explicit consistent decomposition. Original venture pre/post-money and share-count cap table through financing rounds, existing-owner dilution and a clearly specified preferred-versus-common exit waterfall including conversion/participation rules and low-exit boundaries; headline post-money is not automatically pro-rata common fair value. Explain staging/milestones/governance, entrepreneurship opportunity cost and illiquidity. Fund economics: dated LP contributions/distributions, fees, returned capital and a stated carry waterfall; distinguish gross/net results, MOIC/IRR and realized/unrealized marks with source-supported selection/survivorship/vintage caveats. Do not imply universal term sheets, guaranteed private-market outperformance or actual legal/tax rules. Supply self-contained methods, original standard-library lab and all eight solutions.

canonical_spec.title: Distress, restructuring and governance
canonical_spec.outcome: Compare restructuring alternatives and their incentive and valuation consequences.

assignments.scope: Distress, restructuring and governance: distinguish cash-flow distress, economic going-concern viability, balance-sheet negative equity and legal insolvency tests (jurisdiction-specific rather than universal). Use an original finite contractual priority/waterfall case with net liquidation costs, collateral and unsecured deficiency treatment explicitly stipulated; separate recovery divided by face from market-price return. Compare continuation/restructuring with liquidation after new-money and restructuring costs, price new finance consistently and reconcile every old/new claim; value transfers do not become resource gains. Give a closed maturity/refinancing-gap case and consent/governance repair with creditor participation/holdout or coordination constraints; maturity extension changes timing/risk and is not automatic value creation. Stakeholder conflicts, management incentives, fiduciary/process claims only if narrowly sourced and dated; prefer fictional enforceable contracts to unsupported law. Teach full methods before original eight problems; standard-library reproducible lab and scoped primary sources.

canonical_spec.title: Corporate finance integration
canonical_spec.outcome: Defend a financing and investment plan under alternative operating and market conditions.

assignments.scope: Corporate finance integration: original integrated industrial operating/valuation/capital-allocation case tying dated incremental project cash and taxes, reinvestment/continuation economics, financing sources/uses and debt/cash stocks to downside feasibility and shareholder value. Compare at least two feasible policies under explicit base/downside assumptions, covenants and funding dates; do not call unconstrained value maximizing choice feasible if financing fails or confuse expected cash with guaranteed liquidity. Reconcile DCF/equity bridge and conditional comparable evidence, original capital-allocation alternatives and sunk/rights costs, value sensitivity versus funding constraints, and a concise original board-memo recommendation with quantified triggers and uncertainty. Teach an auditable scenario and decision workflow using accepted methods; full worked cases and eight transfer exercises/solutions plus original exact lab. This chapter is instructional integration, not a substitute for the separate volume project and exam package.
